points.quote: Students must never use Generative AI tools to produce content that is presented as their own critical thinking or original creation, whether for assessment or formative work.
points.gist: Students must never use generative AI to produce content presented as their own critical thinking or original creation, in assessed or formative work.

points.quote: Where the University suspects that Generative AI has been used to create assessment content without acknowledgement or authorisation, it reserves the right to invoke formal processes of investigation.
points.gist: The University may start formal investigation where it suspects AI was used to create assessment content without acknowledgement or authorisation.

points.quote: The University does not prohibit the use of Generative AI tools.
points.gist: The University does not prohibit the use of generative AI tools.

points.quote: We encourage students and staff to use AI tools to help get started on tasks, improve their work, and generate new ideas.
points.gist: Students and staff are encouraged to use AI tools to get started, improve work and generate ideas.

points.quote: Students and staff always remain accountable for their final outputs. This includes ensuring that content is appropriate and free of errors.
points.gist: Students and staff remain accountable for final outputs, including that content is appropriate and free of errors.

points.quote: Students and colleagues should state where AI has been used substantially.
points.gist: Students and colleagues should state where AI has been used substantially.

points.quote: Assessment guidance will make clear when the use of Generative AI tools is not permitted, when it is permitted, and under what conditions.
points.gist: Assessment guidance will state when AI use is not permitted, when it is permitted, and under what conditions.

points.quote: Colleagues and students should use AI proportionately, avoid unnecessary regeneration, and are encouraged to choose lower-impact approaches where these meet their needs.
points.gist: Use AI proportionately, avoid unnecessary regeneration, and choose lower-impact approaches where they meet needs.

points.quote: As set out in University IT policies, use of tools (including AI tools) may be monitored.
points.gist: Use of tools, including AI tools, may be monitored under University IT policies.

points.quote: All students will be offered the opportunity to complete an AI training module.
points.gist: All students will be offered the chance to complete an AI training module.

points.quote: The University will make University-provided AI tools available to students and colleagues and will offer training to support their confident and responsible use.
points.gist: The University will make its provided AI tools available to students and colleagues, with training.

points.quote: However, we expect applications to the University (to either study or work here) to be your own, drawing on your skills and experience and expressing your views and values authentically.
points.gist: Applications to study or work at the University are expected to be the applicant's own and authentic.

points.quote: Students are encouraged to speak to the Disability and Inclusion Team, and staff to their line manager and other relevant colleagues, about how University-provided AI tools can be used appropriately as part of a learning agreement or reasonable adjustment.
points.gist: Students are encouraged to speak to the Disability and Inclusion Team about using provided AI tools within a learning agreement or reasonable adjustment.

points.quote: Students and staff should remember that many large language models (LLMs) have been trained on the work of others, including copyrighted and other intellectual property, without permission or payment.
points.gist: Many LLMs have been trained on others' work, including copyrighted material, without permission or payment.
